speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry will consider setting up a drone port to accommodate the rising transport of goods via drones.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have been facilitating this while making sure that associated aviation safety, public safety and security risks are addressed.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have been facilitating trials to better understand the technologies and the implementation and safety issues.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, could the Minister share an update on the regulatory framework, whether the Ministry is forward planning the regulatory framework for a future where, maybe a few years down the road, drones may be widely used in the logistics industry?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Indeed, we are not alone in trying out these various technologies and their applications.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Yes, I am familiar with the Rwanda project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Last year, at the Venice Biennale, the British architect Norman Foster set up a pilot drone port.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: His idea was to set up one, preferably using recyclable materials.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Out of that drone port, you can deliver drugs, medicine and so on to different parts of Africa.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Someone sort of picked up the idea and decided to do it in Rwanda.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Elsewhere in the US, UK and Europe, there are many such experiments being tested out.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: UPS is trying out mobile drone ports by using the roof of their UPS vans so that you can move around and launch your drones off the roof-top of your van.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Singapore, ourselves, should be at the forefront of all these and that explains our proof-of-concept project with Airbus.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Do not forget that to run a trial is not cheap.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As there are many such ideas, our job is to take a good look, select the better ones, especially those which can bring benefits for Singaporeans or help build capabilities among our companies.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The third part about regulations, the answer is also yes.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I have said, it has impact on safety, security and so on.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: My predecessor brought the Bill to this House.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As technology makes progress, we have to keep on tweaking the regulations.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Problem in the sense of the downside impact of the technology; but the upside potential is huge.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The key is how to tap upside potential, while minimising downside effect.
